note.explanation: LARP is a tool for trying out algorithms: you provide inputs, run the instructions, and observe the outputs. It uses simple commands such as START, READ, WRITE, IF...THEN...ELSE, and END.
examples: An even-or-odd algorithm reads a number and displays whether it is even or odd.
A salary algorithm can calculate annual salary and display whether tax applies.
note.checkAnswer: LARP helps you run algorithms and see how different inputs affect their outputs.
note.simple: LARP is like a practice space where you can run an algorithm and see what it does.

note.title: Practising algorithms with LARP
steps: Use READ to get input and WRITE to display messages or results.
Use IF...THEN...ELSE when the algorithm must make a decision.
Run the algorithm with different inputs and check its outputs.

mcqs.stem: Which command begins a LARP algorithm?
rationales: Incorrect: READ is used to input values, not begin the algorithm.
Incorrect: WRITE displays messages or results; it does not begin the algorithm.
Correct: A LARP algorithm begins with START.
Incorrect: ENDIF closes a conditional structure, not the whole algorithm.

options: To display a message or result
mcqs.stem: What is the purpose of the LARP command WRITE?
rationales: Correct: WRITE displays messages or results.
Incorrect: READ is used to input a value.
Incorrect: START begins the algorithm.
Incorrect: ENDIF finishes the IF structure.

mcqs.stem: Which LARP command is used to input a value?
rationales: Incorrect: WRITE displays information.
Correct: READ inputs a value for the algorithm to use.
Incorrect: END finishes the algorithm.
Incorrect: IF begins a decision condition.

mcqs.stem: Which standard flowchart symbol represents a decision?
rationales: Incorrect: A rectangle represents a process.
Correct: A diamond represents a decision.
Incorrect: A parallelogram represents input or output.
Incorrect: A circle is not the standard decision symbol described here.

mcqs.stem: Which LARP structure is used to handle decision-making?
rationales: Incorrect: START and END mark the beginning and ending of the algorithm.
Incorrect: READ and WRITE handle input and output.
Correct: IF...THEN...ELSE is used for decision-making.
Incorrect: THEN and ENDIF are parts of the conditional structure, but the complete decision form is IF...THEN...ELSE.

options: To make complex coding syntax harder
To see how algorithms process data by running them
To replace every flowchart with a picture
To prevent learners from testing different inputs
mcqs.stem: How does LARP help learners understand algorithms?
rationales: Incorrect: LARP uses a simplified approach rather than making syntax harder.
Correct: Running algorithms lets learners see how they process data and produce results.
Incorrect: LARP can execute algorithms, including those developed from flowcharts; it does not replace every flowchart with a picture.
Incorrect: LARP helps learners see the effects of different inputs.

mcqs.stem: Which command ends a complete LARP algorithm?
rationales: Correct: END marks the end of a LARP algorithm.
Incorrect: ENDIF closes an IF conditional structure.
Incorrect: ELSE introduces the alternative branch of a conditional.
Incorrect: WRITE displays information and does not end the algorithm.

By trying different inputs, learners can compare the outputs and check whether the logic works.

If a result is incorrect, the learner can check the condition and the messages in the two branches, then improve the algorithm.

explain.title: What LARP means
explain.body: LARP stands for Logic of Algorithms for resolution of Problems. It is an interactive way to learn how algorithms work by running them and seeing their results.

explain.title: LARP commands
explain.body: A LARP algorithm starts with START and ends with END. READ inputs values, WRITE displays messages or results, and IF...THEN...ELSE handles decisions; ENDIF closes the decision.

explain.title: Why learners use LARP
explain.body: LARP helps you understand algorithms, see how different inputs affect outputs, and practise writing and improving algorithms.

explain.title: Flowcharts in LARP
explain.body: Flowcharts show algorithm steps with standard symbols: rectangles for processes, diamonds for decisions, and parallelograms for input/output. A flowchart can be translated into LARP commands and executed to check its logic.

mistakes: Writing the wrong expansion of LARP or leaving out the word resolution.
Confusing READ, which inputs a value, with WRITE, which displays information.
Forgetting START, END, or ENDIF in the algorithm.
Writing a condition but not providing an output for both the IF and ELSE cases.
Assuming a flowchart is executed directly without translating it into LARP syntax as described in the section.
